title: Data-Driven Prediction of NaCl-Type Entropy-Stabilized Oxide Compositions from First-Principles and Supervised Learning
authors: Sebastien Junier, Celine Barreteau, David Berardan, Yann-Andrev Kerneur, Jean-Claude Crivello
abstract: Entropy-stabilized oxides (ESOs) open access to vast multicomponent compositional spaces, but identifying promising candidates remains challenging because of the large number of possible mixtures and the need to assess their stability against competing phases. In this work, we develop a high-throughput computational framework to screen equimolar quinary ESOs in the NaCl structure type by combining density functional theory (DFT), special quasirandom structures (SQS), convex-hull thermodynamics, and supervised machine learning. A consistent reference database of binary and ternary ordered oxides, including disordered phases such as all binary cation combinations in the NaCl-type oxide, is first constructed using GGA and meta-GGA calculations. Quinary disordered phases are then described by SQS supercells and used to train machine-learning models that predict the distance to the convex hull and the corresponding stabilization temperature over the full set of 4368 possible equimolar quinary compositions generated from 16 cation species. Among the tested models, an optimized multilayer perceptron provides the best predictive performance, with a test error of about 4 kJ/mol, while requiring explicit DFT calculations for only about 10% of the quinary systems. Comparison with experimental synthesis tests and computed decomposition paths further shows that the approach captures the main stability trends and the dominant competing phases, although absolute stabilization temperatures remain affected by systematic thermodynamic approximations. These results establish an efficient route for the data-driven exploration of multicomponent oxides and provide practical guidance for the experimental search for new ESOs.
summary: This work presents a data-driven computational framework to explore Entropy-Stabilized Oxides by combining DFT calculations, SQS modeling of disorder, and supervised machine learning. The method efficiently screens thousands of potential oxide compositions to predict their thermodynamic stability relative to competing phases. This establishes an efficient route for the materials discovery process in complex solid-state chemistry.
main_problem: The challenge of identifying stable, promising candidates within the vast compositional space of Entropy-Stabilized Oxides (ESOs) due to complex phase stability assessment.
main_result: A high-throughput computational framework was developed that efficiently screens thousands of quinary ESO compositions using machine learning predictions, requiring explicit DFT calculations for only about 10% of the systems tested.
method: The approach combines Density Functional Theory (DFT) with Special Quasirandom Structures (SQS) to model disorder, and then trains supervised machine learning models (like MLP) on these results to predict thermodynamic stability metrics.
model_or_system: The study focuses on equimolar quinary ESOs in the NaCl structure type, involving 16 selected cation species. Stability is assessed by calculating the formation enthalpy relative to the convex hull ($\Delta	ext{hull}H$) and determining a finite-temperature stabilization point ($T_{	ext{stab}}$).
key_observables: Formation enthalpy ($\Delta fH$), distance to the convex hull ($\Delta	ext{hull}H$), and stabilization temperature ($T_{	ext{stab}}$).
important_parameters: The system size involves 4368 possible quinary compositions; ML models achieve a test error of $\sim 4 	ext{ kJ}\cdot	ext{mol}^{-1}$.
main_assumptions: Absolute stabilization temperatures are affected by systematic thermodynamic approximations, and the method relies on extrapolations from smaller systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate SQS modeling (pair cluster distribution), ML model performance curves (prediction vs. learning), and tables list predicted stability trends for various quinary compositions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds a reference database using DFT/SQS, develops thermodynamic criteria ($\Delta fH$, $\Delta	ext{hull}G$), trains supervised ML models on this data, and applies the resulting framework to screen large compositional spaces.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science, the core methodology—combining high-dimensional physical simulation (DFT/SQS) with advanced machine learning for predictive screening in complex parameter spaces—is highly relevant to developing ML potentials or predicting quantum phases in strongly correlated systems.
